guideTitle: Best Robot Vacuums for Pet Hair (2026)
metaTitle: Best Robot Vacuums for Pet Hair (2026)
metaDescription: Six robot vacuums for pet hair compared on brush design, dock bag size, edge cleaning and upkeep, from rubber-roller flagships to a budget tangle-free port.
expertTake: The iRobot Roomba Max 715 Pet is the top pick because its twin rubber rollers and 90-day dock are built for shedding. The ILIFE V2 is the value pick, a slim tangle-free robot that costs very little. Owners of heavy shedders should skip budget bin-only robots for daily use, since they fill within minutes.
introParagraphs: Pet hair is both a volume problem and a mechanical one. A shedding dog puts out far more hair than a person, and long strands wrap around spinning brushes until the motor labors. A good pet robot has to pick the hair up, keep it off the shaft and then store a lot of it.

That is why the bin and dock matter as much as the brush. A small bin fills within a single room, and a dock that holds a month of fur turns a chore into a quarterly job. This guide ranks six machines on how they collect, release and store hair.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Max 715 Pet, 30,000 Pa, dual rubber brushes, 90-day dock

specList.label: Brushes
specList.value: Dual rubber anti-tangle plus side brush

products.description:
The Max 715 Pet is built around two rubber rollers that flex and stay in contact with the floor, which is the gentlest way to lift pet hair without winding it. Patented anti-tangle rubber is the key feature, because rubber blades have no bristles for strands to snag. A side brush sweeps the edges, and the dock empties the bin automatically for up to 90 days.

Its 30,000 Pa label is the highest here, and the listing describes 4X more power-lifting suction than an earlier design, but as always that is a peak figure. The rollers matter more. Compared with the Shark Matrix Plus it trades mopping for a bigger bag interval, 90 days against 30 days, and it sits at a high price tier.

Care is simple. Pull the rollers every couple of weeks and wipe them, because rubber lets you do it in seconds. Replace the dock bag when the app asks, and keep spare rollers and a side brush on hand, since rubber wears and flattens over a year of heavy use. A set of spare rollers lets you swap one while the other dries after a wash, which keeps the schedule running.
products.bestFor: Homes with shedding dogs and cats that want the least tangling.
pros: Twin rubber rollers do not wind hair
cons: Rubber rollers wear and need replacing

products.name: eufy E25, 20,000 Pa, zero-tangle brush, HydroJet roller mop, 75-day bag

specList.label: Mop
specList.value: HydroJet roller, refreshed twice per second

products.description:
The E25 handles pet hair on both the dry and wet sides. A zero-tangle brush design collects strands, an extendable side brush pulls debris out of corners and a roller mop refreshed with clean water twice per second picks up the paw prints and dander that survive the vacuum. Wet hair that a flat pad would smear gets lifted by the roller.

It carries 20,000 Pa and a 3 L bag good for about 75 days, which is less than the Roomba Max 715 Pet, but it adds a real mop. If your dog tracks mud, the roller mop is the reason to prefer it. It sits at a high price tier because of the wash dock.

The dock washes the roller and dries it with hot air at about 50 C. Empty the dirty tank, clear the roller ends of strands and replace the bag when the app asks. Keep the mop off thick pet beds. A damp roller on a fleece bed leaves a wet patch, so mark pet bed areas as no-go zones in the app.
products.bestFor: Pet homes with muddy paws and a mix of floors.
pros: Roller mop lifts wet pet hair and mud
Dock washes and dries the roller
cons: Bag interval shorter than the Roomba

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus UR2650WS, Matrix Clean, sonic mopping, CleanEdge, HEPA base
products.description:
The Matrix Plus tackles pet hair with method. Matrix Clean makes several grid passes over each strip, which lifts embedded hair out of carpet that a single pass leaves behind. CleanEdge Detect uses bursts of air and corner recognition to clear edges where fur piles up, and sonic mopping vibrates a pad on hard floors.

Its HEPA base holds up to 30 days, shorter than the Roomba Max 715 Pet, and the sonic pad is lighter duty than the eufy roller. It sits at a mid price tier. The grid passes are the reason it ranks among the top for carpeted homes with pets.

Empty the base roughly monthly and wash the HEPA filter by the maker schedule. Clear the brush end caps weekly and rinse the sonic pad after each wet run. In a house with two cats the HEPA filter is the part that clogs first, so it earns a reminder on the calendar.
products.bestFor: Carpeted pet homes that want grid passes and HEPA.
pros: Grid passes lift hair from carpet
cons: 30 day base is the shortest here

products.name: Roborock Q7 M5+, 10,000 Pa, JawScrapers comb, 2.7 L bag, 7 to 9 weeks
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ attacks hair with a comb. The JawScrapers main brush has teeth along the roller that strip strands as it turns, and a zero-tangle side brush protects the other end. A 2.7 L sealed bag dock covers 7 to 9 weeks, and LiDAR plans the route.

It costs much less than the Roomba Max 715 Pet and has a smaller bag, so heavy shedders fill it faster. The vibrating mop pad handles light wet work. For a moderate-shedding home, the comb is a proven and cheaper design.

Pull the main brush weekly and cut away strands the comb missed. Replace the sealed bag when full and rinse the mop pad. The shared Roborock platform makes brushes easy to find. Because it relies on a comb, it is also worth checking the teeth for bent tips every few months.
products.bestFor: Moderate-shedding homes that want a proven comb brush on a budget.
pros: Comb brush strips hair as it spins
Sealed 2.7 L bag lasts 7 to 9 weeks
cons: Smaller bag fills quickly with heavy shedders

products.name: ILIFE A30 Pro, 10,000 Pa, 2.5 L station, 5 bags, 280-day quote, LiDAR
products.description:
The A30 Pro is the pet-hair robot that ships with its own supply. Five dust bags come in the box and the listing quotes up to 280 days of hands-free use from a 2.5 L station. For a household with fur everywhere, the bags matter, because a station fills faster than the quote.

Its 10,000 Pa is a peak, and the brush design is the same family as other budget laser robots. Below the Roborock Q7 M5+ in price, it still includes a mop. The 280 day figure is a best case, so expect shorter intervals with a shedding dog.

Change the bag when the app prompts, rinse the pad and clear the brush weekly. The extra bags mean the first year of upkeep is paid for. Its mop is a plain attachment, so keep it off pet beds and rugs.
products.bestFor: Pet homes that want bags included and a laser map.
pros: Five dust bags in the box
cons: 2.5 L station fills faster than quoted with shedders

products.name: ILIFE V2, tangle-free suction port, 2.99 in slim, remote, 120 minutes
products.description:
The V2 deals with pet hair by avoiding the brushroll problem altogether. A tangle-free suction port, described for pet owners on hard floors, pulls hair in without a spinning bristle roller to wrap. At 2.99 in tall it also reaches under beds where fur collects, and a remote runs it without Wi-Fi.

It is the cheapest machine here and has a small bin, so a shedding dog fills it quickly. Against the Roborock Q7 M5+ it has no dock, no map and much less capacity. It suits light shedders on hard floors or a bedroom.

Rinse the filter, clear the suction port and empty the bin after every run. With no roller, there is little to cut free, which is the main attraction. Its bin is small enough to see through, so you will notice fur piling up and can empty it before suction drops.
products.bestFor: Light shedders on hard floors and under-bed dust on a tight budget.
cons: Small bin fills fast with a shedding pet

buyingCriteria.explanation: Three designs fight hair differently. Rubber rollers like the Roomba Max 715 Pet have no bristles to snag, a comb like the Roborock JawScrapers strips strands as it turns and a roller-less port like the ILIFE V2 avoids the problem. Choose by how much hair and how long it is, and expect to check any design weekly.

A dog can fill a small bin in one room. Docks like the Roomba Max 715 Pet at up to 90 days and the ILIFE A30 Pro with five bags buy time, and the V2 bin fills fast. Treat quoted days as best cases for a shedding pet.

Pet hair gathers along baseboards and under furniture edges. The Shark Matrix Plus uses CleanEdge Detect, and the eufy E25 has an extendable side brush. A robot that leaves the edges behind will leave a hair line.
A damp paw print with hair is a mop problem. A roller mop like the eufy E25 lifts it, and flat pads smear it. If your pet tracks mud, favour a roller.
Embedded hair needs multiple passes. The Shark Matrix Plus drives a grid, which lifts fur from pile that a single pass leaves. On carpet, passes matter more than a bigger Pa number.
Pet dander is a fine particle that a leaky robot returns to the air. The Shark Matrix Plus lists a HEPA base. If anyone in the house is allergic, check how the dock is sealed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rubber, comb and roller-less designs. The Roomba Max 715 Pet and Roborock Q7 M5+ lead for long strands. Bristle rollers scored lowest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bag sizes and bags in the box, such as five on the ILIFE A30 Pro. Pet homes fill bins quickly. Capacity weighed heavily. A robot that cannot hold a week of fur forces daily emptying, which defeats the purpose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edge and carpet
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at edge tools and grid passes, like CleanEdge and Matrix Clean on the Shark. Hair gathers at edges and in pile. Models without either scored lower. A robot that skips edges leaves a fur line along every wall, which is the most visible failure in a pet home.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wet cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the eufy roller, Shark sonic pad and Roborock vibrating pad. Rollers lift wet hair best. Dry-only machines were judged on dry performance. Models with both a mop and a brush that tangles were not rescued by the mop.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed repeated owner reports on wrapped rollers, full bins and pet accidents. Patterns outweighed single complaints. Models that jam on long hair were marked down. The recurring complaint was a robot stopping on a hair clog in the middle of the night, which is a design limit more than bad luck.

cards.label: Rubber
cards.text: The Roomba Max 715 Pet uses twin rubber rollers that resist wrap and wipe clean. Rubber wears and costs more to replace.

cards.label: Comb
cards.text: The Roborock Q7 M5+ strips hair with teeth along the roller. It is cheaper and needs a weekly trim.

howToChoose.note: Pick rubber for heavy shedders and comb for moderate ones. Neither design helps if the bin is full, so decide the dock first.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A big bag, a brush you can clear in seconds and a schedule that runs daily. Plan to empty the dock early. A bag that feels heavy in the hand is full, whatever the app says.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Roomba Max 715 Pet has the longest dock interval and rubber rollers. The ILIFE A30 Pro adds spare bags.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a heavy shedder or allergies. The Roomba Max 715 Pet and Shark Matrix Plus address both.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Shedding is light. The ILIFE V2 or Roborock Q7 M5+ cover it for less.

maintenance.why: Pet hair gathers at the end caps even on anti-tangle designs. Rubber wipes clean, and bristles need scissors.
Fur fills bags faster than the quote. Check weekly in spring and autumn.
Dander clogs filters. Dry it fully.
Wet hair and mud foul pads quickly. Dry them in open air.
Hair winds around wheel axles and cuts traction. Pull it out with tweezers.

faq.q: Which brush is best for pet hair?
faq.a: Rubber rollers resist wrap best, and combs do well on moderate shedding. A roller-less port avoids the problem on hard floors. Check any brush weekly. Hair wraps even on good designs once strands exceed the length of the roller, so a weekly look is cheap insurance.

faq.q: Do I need a self-empty dock?
faq.a: For a shedding pet, yes. A bin fills in one room, so a dock like the Roomba Max 715 Pet saves daily chores. Bags are a cost. Over a year the bag bill is small next to the time saved.

faq.q: Will a robot clean pet accidents?
faq.a: No. Wet messes can spread and clog brushes. Clean them by hand first. Dried accidents also leave a smell that a robot will spread on its wheels. Some models recognise waste, which needs a camera.

faq.q: Does suction matter for pet hair?
faq.a: Less than the brush. Hair sits on top of hard floors, and carpet needs agitation. Peak Pa is a poor guide. Choose by brush and bag instead.

faq.q: How often should I empty the dock?
faq.a: Check monthly, or weekly in shedding season. Many owners find a fixed day of the month easier than watching the app. The quoted days are best cases. A smelly dock needs emptying sooner.

faq.q: Is a mop useful for pet homes?
faq.a: A roller mop lifts paw prints and dander well. Flat pads smear. Keep rugs marked as no-mop zones. Wet fur on a rug is hard to dry and easy to avoid.
